skill.displayName: 弱电智能化投标决策-安防监控项目投标评估

llm.summary: This bid-analysis skill is coherent, but it stores account credentials, uses device-derived registration data, and creates shareable reports with signed links, so it needs user review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses network access and local output, but it can collect platform, CPU architecture, and a MAC-derived hash for registration, and it writes HTML reports containing raw signed URLs by default.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer hook, dependency install, remote code retrieval, or startup persistence was found; the packaged Python script is a local HTML renderer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation is broad for related procurement questions, and the skill instructs agents to hide technical API details from users while still making external calls and local writes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists API keys in ~/.zlbx/config.json, reuses them in later sessions, and can generate signed auto-login/recharge links when quota is exhausted.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core bid-analysis workflow matches the stated purpose, but account auto-registration, recharge-link generation, upgrade acknowledgements, and signed-link report sharing expand the skill beyond analysis into account and billing-adjacent behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill using the Zhiliaobiaoxun API, storing an API key under ~/.zlbx/config.json, collecting a hashed MAC address for trial registration when you consent, and generating local HTML reports that may contain signed links. Preconfiguring ZLBX_API_KEY avoids the auto-registration path, and generated reports should be shared only with intended recipients.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced render_report.py file was present and fully inspected; it renders local HTML and does not fetch or execute remote payloads.
[SC3] expected: The long base64 blob in render_report.py is an embedded PNG logo used in the HTML report, not decoded and executed code.
[P2] expected: The package/request identity blocks are visible markdown directives for API headers and upgrade notice handling; they are not hidden code, though the display-acknowledgement side effect is under-disclosed to users.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Auto-registration and account recovery support API onboarding, but the full credential lifecycle and recharge flow are broader than a bid-decision analysis task.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The MAC-derived hash, persisted API key, absolute report path, and raw signed URLs are disclosed in the artifacts, but they create privacy and sharing risks that are not necessary for the analytical output itself.
[E1] unexpected: External posting of registration data is consent-gated and limited to the vendor domain, but device-derived data transmission is separate from ordinary bid-analysis queries.
[RA2] unexpected: The artifact shows local API-key persistence, but not system backdoors, scheduled tasks, or autonomous background execution.
[LP3] expected: Local HTML report creation is part of the stated reporting feature, but it is default behavior and should be clearly user-controlled.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad activation language could route loosely related requests into this external API workflow unexpectedly.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese report wording appears aligned with the Chinese-language service and target workflow, not a security issue by itself.
